data.title: Australian Funds Add Bets on Materials, Tech; Pare Back on Health — Market Talk
data.description: Australian fund managers last month reduced their underweight position in materials and added to their overweight one in tech, says Morgan Stanley. The changes were funded by cuts to bets on healthcare, which remains managers' largest overweight exposure, MS says. CSL remains the top-held stock in healthcare, followed by ResMed, says the bank. In materials, funds added holdings of BHP but cut Rio Tinto, it says. In tech, Xero was the largest stock holding for the sector, it says. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)

data.title: Core inflation in Japan's capital accelerates in November
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nov core CPI rises 2.9% yr/yr vs forecast +3.0%
  • Index excluding fresh food, energy rises 2.5% yr/yr
  • BOJ next meets Dec 17-18, markets expect rate hike to 1.5%

By Leika Kihara and Takahiko Wada

Annual core inflation in Japan's capital accelerated in November and stayed above the central bank's 2% target for three straight months, highlighting mounting price pressure and bolstering the case for a near-term interest rate hike.

The data, widely regarded as a leading indicator of nationwide trends, will be among factors the Bank of Japan scrutinises in deciding whether to raise interest rates at its next two-day policy meeting ending on December 18.

The core consumer price index, which includes prices of fuel but not fresh food, in Tokyo rose 2.9% in November from a year earlier, data showed on Friday, compared with the median market forecast of 3.0%. It followed a 2.6% gain in October.

An index stripping away the effect of volatile fresh food and fuel prices, which is closely watched by the BOJ as a more accurate gauge of trend inflation, rose 2.5% in November after a 2.6% gain in October, the data showed.

data.title: Gold Fortunes Tied to Stocks in Near Term — Market Talk
data.description: Near-term pressure on gold may persist until equities stabilize, says HSBC analyst James Steel. "Continued equity market weakness puts gold at risk of breaking the next major support level at $3,400/oz," he says. Still, gold appears undervalued and any sign of central-bank buying could arrest declines, Steel says. In silver, which has lost two-thirds of its value since notching record highs earlier in the year, there are reasons to expect a bounce. He cites prices around $40/oz, which are "not historically expensive," and expectations of an annual deficit. "Similarly, the PGMs are at levels that long-term investors can regard as good value," says Steel, referring to platinum group metals. Spot gold is little changed at $3,566.25 an ounce. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)

data.title: Brent crude crosses $96 a barrel mark after Houthis attack key Saudi refinery
data.description:
Crude oil prices have edged higher during a thin volume holiday trading session on Friday, November 27, after an attack on a key refinery in Saudi Arabia.

Brent crude traded above the $96 a barrel mark for the January contracts, having already gained more than 6% in the previous two sessions. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) or the US crude futures for the January settlement are also trading 1.5% higher in early trading in Asia, close to the $85 a barrel mark.

Saudi Arabia's press agency reported citing an unnamed Energy Ministry source that the Iran-backed Houthis attacked the Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast, halting some operations, killing one worker, and injuring many others.

The Jazan refinery has a capcity of 4,00,000 barrels per day and the attacks mark another blow to the oil infrastructure in the region that has been subject to multiple attacks in the recent days. Houthis on Wednesday also claimed to have attacked the key Ras Tanura refinery, which has a capacity of 5,00,000 barrels per day, a claim that the Saudi administration has not confirmed yet.

According to the UK Maritime Trade Operations, another tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, while Iran claimed, without independent confirmation, that several vessels hit mines in the key waterway.

Despite the attacks, shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has increased in November, as per data from Vortexa. These flows, coupled with the International Energy Agency (IEA) forecasting an oil surplus this quarter, have kept prices in check despite the recent attacks.

Trading volumes are expected to remain thin Thursday because of the US Thanksgiving holiday, which could exaggerate prices moves. West Texas Intermediate trades will be booked for Friday settlement.

(With Inputs From Agencies)

data.title: Powerful Storm Hits East Coast, Scrambling Thanksgiving Plans — WSJ
data.description:
By Victoria Albert

A major storm is scrambling Thanksgiving Day plans along the East Coast, with heavy winds and rain causing power outages, flight cancellations and the postponement of Macy's annual holiday parade.

The National Weather Service said widespread coastal flooding was under way along the mid-Atlantic and New England coastline, with "significant inundation" in Virginia, the Delaware Bay and parts of the Chesapeake Bay and southern New Jersey coast. Forecasters warned to expect flooded structures and impassable roads, as well as wind gusts of up to 60 mph along the coast and 50 mph further inland.

About 1 to 3 inches of rain are expected in the region, with the possibility of scattered flash flooding.

Footage from local news showed heavy flooding on some Virginia roads. Rich Otto, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service, said some parts of the state have already seen 2 to 4 inches of rain, though rainfall there is expected to ease as the storm crawls north.

As of early Thursday afternoon, more than 550,000 people were without power along the East Coast and mid-Atlantic, according to Poweroutage.us. The outages were concentrated in Maryland and Virginia, where energy-provider Dominion said broken utility poles and large trees on power lines meant it could be days before power was restored in some areas.

"Outages are especially difficult on a holiday, and we appreciate your patience as our crews work to get the lights back on," the utility said on social media.

Another 123,000 power outages were reported in Missouri, according to Poweroutage.us, after several inches of snow fell on the eastern side of the state. Some areas, including Ste. Genevieve, Mo., saw as much as 14 inches of snow, according to the National Weather Service.

Roughly 1,600 flights within, into or out of the U.S. have been delayed, and more than 400 have been canceled, according to flight-data specialist FlightAware. The hardest-hit airport thus far is Washington Dulles International Airport in Virginia.

In New York City, where fears of severe weather forced officials to postpone the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, wind gusts exceeding 30 mph were recorded across all five boroughs — including a 56 mph gust at LaGuardia Airport in Queens. The city's emergency-management department warned residents to secure loose outdoor items and use caution around trees and scaffolding.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani warned the city could see wind gusts as high as 65 mph. "If you're traveling, give yourself extra time," Mamdani warned Wednesday night. "And remember: No destination is worth risking your safety."

Write to Victoria Albert at victoria.albert@wsj.com

data.title: Patrys Begins Dosing of Second Cohort in RLS-2202 Delirium Drug Trial
data.description:
Patrys Limited has administered the first doses to healthy volunteers in the second cohort of its Phase 1a clinical trial of RLS-2202 (quetiapine), an injectable treatment candidate for delirium.

The study will directly compare the intravenous formulation of quetiapine with the established oral version of the antipsychotic in 12 participants.

Patrys intends to use the results to draw on existing safety data for oral quetiapine under the US Food and Drug Administration’s 505(b)(2) regulatory pathway, which could reduce the time and cost of bringing RLS-2202 to market.

Final dosing remains on track for December 2026, with initial results expected in the first quarter of 2027.

Hospital Treatment Gap

Delirium is an acute disturbance of brain function that affects up to 80% of mechanically ventilated patients in intensive care units and is associated with longer hospital stays, higher costs, and increased mortality.

The FDA has yet to approve a medicine for either the prevention or treatment of delirium, leaving clinicians reliant on off-label antipsychotics.

Many critically ill patients cannot reliably take oral medication, prompting Patrys to develop an IV formulation intended to provide rapid and controllable treatment in hospitalised patients.

“With no FDA-approved treatment for delirium, we believe a fast-acting intravenous option could make a real difference for ICU patients and the clinicians who care for them,” chief executive officer Dr Samantha South said.

“With GMP clinical supply released for Cohort 2 and full bioanalytical validation now underway, the key building blocks are in place to deliver Cohort 2 efficiently and to drive RLS-2202 through Phase 1 and into the next stage of development.”

Two Delivery Methods

The first group of volunteers will remain at the clinical trial site until they have completed both dosing periods, with recruitment continuing for the second group to fill the cohort.

Each participant will receive both formulations, separated by a four-day washout period, allowing researchers to compare drug exposure while reducing the influence of individual differences in metabolism.

IV administration can result in higher peak drug concentrations and a faster onset than oral administration, and the study will assess whether RLS-2202 introduces any additional safety concerns in healthy volunteers.

Patrys intends to use the Phase 1a data in discussions with the FDA in 2027 on the design of its next study involving ICU patients with delirium.

Clinical Supply and Testing

Patrys has delivered a batch of RLS-2202 manufactured under current good manufacturing practice standards to CMAX Clinical Research after completing quality control testing, packaging and labelling.

The batch met all agreed specifications for human administration, with a stability program underway to support a shelf life covering the current and subsequent studies.

Following preliminary testing using samples from the first cohort, Patrys has begun full validation of its laboratory method for measuring blood concentrations of quetiapine and its active by-product norquetiapine.

The resulting measurements will inform decisions on safe dose increases and the selection of doses for future patient studies.

Patrys expects to complete participant screening and enrolment as well as validation of the laboratory method for second cohort samples before the end of 2026.

data.title: Panther Minerals Adopts Semi-Annual Reporting
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / Panther Minerals Inc. ("Panther" or the "Company") announces that it has elected to rely on Coordinated Blanket Order 51-933 - Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers (the "Order") and move to semi-annual financial reporting ("SAR"). This news release is being filed pursuant to Coordinated Blanket Order 51 - 933 Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers.

The Order allows eligible venture issuers listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "CSE") to voluntarily move from a quarterly to a semi-annual financial reporting framework. The Company's fiscal year ends on June 30. Under the SAR pilot program, the Company will be exempt from filing interim financial reports and related Management's Discussion & Analysis (MD&A) for its first and third quarters.

  • Interim Period: The Company will not file an interim report for the first quarter (Q1) ending September 30 and the third quarter (Q3) ending March 31; and
  • Ongoing Reporting: The Company will continue to file audited financial statements (due within 120 days of June 30) and six-month interim financial reports (due within 60 days of December 31).

The Company confirms it meets the pilot program's eligibility criteria, which include being a venture issuer with annual revenues of no more than $10 million, having been a reporting issuer in at least one Canadian jurisdiction for at least 12 months and having ﬁled all required periodic and timely continuous disclosure documents.

The ﬁrst period for which the Company will not ﬁle an interim ﬁnancial report and related MD&A will be for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026.

About Panther Minerals Inc.

Panther Minerals Inc. is a North American critical minerals exploration company. Its portfolio includes the Rubidium Ridge lithium-cesium-tantalum property near Atikokan, Ontario, the East Brouillan property in Quebec, and an option to acquire a 100% interest in the Mesa Top uranium property in New Mexico. Panther trades on the CSE under the symbol PURR, on the OTCQB under the symbol GLIOF and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under the symbol 2BC.
